newsitem.title: UK: Nordic American shares to start trading Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: Nordic American shares to start trading Oct 1.

text.p: Shares in Nordic American Tanker Shipping Ltd will start trading in New York with a secondary listing in Oslo on October 1, the tanker company said on Thursday.
Herbjorn Hansson, Nordic American chairman, said the shares would start trading following the conversion of Nordic American warrants on September 30.
"After conversion they will be trading both in New York and Oslo," Hansson told Reuters.
The Oslo Stock Exchange said on Wednesday it had approved an application from Nordic American for a secondary listing.
"We have formally renewed the application," said Hansson. "The plan was laid out in the original prospectus when we sold the warrants two years ago."

A prospectus for the warrant conversion is currently under preparation. Hansson said he expected the company would come to the market with a capitalisation of $175 million to $180 million and was confident the shares would perform strongly, buoyed by optimism over an improved outlook for tanker freight rates.
Nordic American was set up in 1995 to finance the construction of three 150,000 dwt Suezmax tankers for British Petroleum at Samsung Heavy Industries Co Ltd in South Korea.
Investors paid $58.7 million for Nordic American warrants, with the cash used to make down-payments on the three tankers.

Warrant holders will be able to exercise their right to convert the warrants into shares this September at $10.21 each. This will raise a further $119.8 million to meet delivery payments on the three ships.

At the end of last month, Nordic American said it was confident that rising tanker freight rates would ensure higher dividends to shareholders than the minimum guaranteed under the long-term BP charters.
The first vessel, British Harrier, was delivered to Nordic American on August 4.
Nordic American is managed by Ugland Nordic Shipping ASA.
